root_cause: The generic .github/workflows/ shared-path fallback classified an unmapped workflow definition as shared executable work. That activated every delivery lane, including website/browser, even when the changed workflow had no website runtime impact.
prevention: Explicit workflow ownership remains authoritative. An unmapped .github/workflows/* definition now defaults to the backend control-plane lane only; explicit website workflow paths still select the website lane. Regression tests cover the powerhouse-ci-intelligence workflow and a future unmapped workflow.

evidence.observed_failure: PR #4005 workflow-only changes activated website/browser through the generic .github/workflows shared-path fallback.
evidence.expected_prevention: Generic workflow-only changes select backend control-plane unless an explicit workflow owner selects another lane; website/browser remains off for non-website changes.

historical_replay.scenario: PR #4005 changes an unmapped control-plane workflow definition together with explicitly owned CI workflows.
historical_replay.expected: The unmapped .github/workflows/* path defaults to backend control-plane, explicit owners keep their lane, and website/browser stays disabled unless a website-owned path is present.

historical_replay.scenario: A future workflow file has no explicit ownership entry.
historical_replay.expected: Fail closed to backend control-plane only; do not activate portal, website, or automation implicitly.
